NDT software in Jacksonville: a port, navy and power market

Jacksonville's inspection work starts at the water. JAXPORT runs cargo terminals at Blount Island, Dames Point and Talleyrand along the St. Johns River, and petroleum products arrive by ship to the fuel terminals that supply much of northeast Florida. Crowley is headquartered in the city, and ship repair yards along the river, including BAE Systems Jacksonville Ship Repair, handle commercial and navy vessels. Naval Station Mayport sits at the river mouth, NAS Jacksonville hosts Fleet Readiness Center Southeast for aircraft maintenance, and Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay is just over the Georgia line. Boeing has an aircraft maintenance operation at Cecil Airport. On the power side, JEA's Northside Generating Station is one of the larger plants in the region. Add fabrication shops on the Westside, structural work for a fast-growing metro, and marine work up the coast to Brunswick and Savannah.

That makes the typical Jacksonville NDT contractor part marine, part industrial. Hull thickness gauging, weld inspection on ship repair, and MT and UT for class surveys sit next to tank and piping work at terminals and power plant outages. The regulators and authorities shaping that work include the US Coast Guard, classification societies such as ABS, DNV and Lloyd's Register, Florida's Bureau of Radiation Control for radiography licensing (Florida is an NRC Agreement State), PHMSA for pipeline and terminal operators, and the Boiler Safety Program under Florida's State Fire Marshal. Hurricane season adds a scheduling problem few other markets have.

ERP for NDT companies in Jacksonville: the short answer

The Atlantis ERP solution is a fully customized ERP for NDT and inspection companies, set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, whose founder Anoop Rayavarapu is an ASNT NDT Level III. It runs quotes, jobs, technicians, equipment, reports and invoices in one system, and it includes a marine reporting mode built for vessel work. It is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with pricing on request.

For a Jacksonville company, the practical gain is that marine and industrial jobs sit in the same system without forcing one to look like the other. A hull gauging job carries the vessel, the class society and the inspection location; a terminal job carries the tank, the WPS and the client PO. Both draw on the same technician and equipment records and both flow to the same invoicing. Each capability is its own app; see the full list on the ERP apps page. The sections below apply the most important apps to Jacksonville work.

NDT reporting software with a marine mode for Jacksonville vessel work

The NDT Reports app has a marine mode that adds a vessel cover page and photo, inspection location and dates, and merges the classification-society certificate, the inspector's Level II certificate and the calibration certificate into the PDF. For Jacksonville ship repair and class survey work, that turns the report package a surveyor expects into one document instead of a stapled stack.

The class society library includes DNV, ABS, Lloyd's Register, BV, RINA, IRS and ClassNK. Inspection photos lay out in a two-up grid. Across the 17 report types (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday and coating, and computed radiography), the ones Jacksonville crews use most are likely UT thickness, with readings by direction for gauging, MT with technique and particle type for weld repairs, UT with a probe calibration table, and holiday and coating reports for tank and hull coatings. Weld or job lines record defect type and orientation, and each report closes as acceptable, not acceptable or acceptable with remarks, with references to work order, contract, drawing, WPS, procedure and standard.

Reports move through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures and a third-party or authorized inspector name and signature. The offline field app matters more here than almost anywhere: inside a double bottom or a ballast tank there is no signal, so drafts and photos are stored locally and sync later. Versioned company templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML carry your logo, and client Excel formats are filled by mapping fields to cells. See also Digital Twin Reporting Software.

Technician certification tracking software for marine and industrial crews

The Certificates app tracks each technician's certifications by scheme, level and method and sets status automatically: active, expiring soon (90 days), expired or revoked. Because the marine PDF merges the inspector's Level II certificate, keeping that certificate current in the system also keeps your report packages correct.

Schemes include SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN and CSWIP, plus other. Foreign-flag vessels and international owners calling at Jacksonville sometimes ask for ISO 9712, PCN or CSWIP-qualified inspectors, and those certificates are recorded alongside your SNT-TC-1A certifications with their own dates. Each record holds certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, industry sector, OJT hours, training hours, exam results and attachments. Vision tests record near vision at Jaeger J1 or J2, far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner, clinic and expiry.

The employee NDT profile adds radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry. Daily checks create warning tasks 90 days before certification or vision test expiry, and configurable email alerts cover technician certificates, calibration certificates and company certifications such as your ISO registration. Timesheets warn if a technician logs hours without a valid certificate. The software records and reminds; your Level III and written practice decide qualification.

Calibration management software for gauges, flaw detectors and yokes

Asset Management tracks every thickness gauge, flaw detector, yoke, probe and source-related item by serial number with calibration frequency and status. Team Assignments warns when an out-of-calibration item is assigned, and the marine PDF pulls the calibration certificate in automatically, so the instrument record and the report stay in step.

Each item carries equipment type, asset tag, firmware, accessories, assigned person, condition and lifecycle: new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired or disposed. Calibration records hold provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag, result and next due date, and the certificate register stores lab accreditation number, PDF and a valid, expiring or expired status with alerts. Purchase can type vendors as OEM, dealer or calibration lab and link a purchase line to a specific serial.

Salt air and shipyard conditions are hard on equipment. The maintenance log records preventive and corrective work, cleaning, repairs, firmware updates and probe replacements with condition before and after, and the issue and return workflow records condition both ways with supervisor and manager approval. Consumables such as couplant, magnetic particles, contrast paint, penetrant and PPE carry reorder levels and a low-stock flag. Reservations prevent two jobs claiming the same gauge.

Crew dispatch and scheduling software around the St. Johns River

Team Assignments moves each job through planned, dispatched, in field, submitted and closed, with site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates, and blocks double-booking of technicians and equipment serial numbers. Ship repair schedules change at short notice when a vessel's arrival slips, and the dispatch board has to follow.

A Jacksonville crew might be at Blount Island in the morning, a terminal on Talleyrand in the afternoon and a fabricator on the Westside the next day, with a call to Brunswick or Fernandina Beach in between. The availability calendar shows assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable, and blocks overlaps. Approved Time Off feeds the same calendar. Each technician shows current assignment, utilisation percentage and next available date, in calendar, kanban and list views. When a storm closes the port, you can see every affected job and who is free to redeploy once it reopens.

The Fleet app records vehicle purpose, whether the vehicle can carry radioactive sources, transport licence number and expiry, and assignment to a project and driver with dates and mileage, which ties the radiography truck to the right job and the right person.

Procedure control for class surveys and industrial clients

The Procedures app keeps your NDT procedures in a controlled register with document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard, acceptance criteria and the text or file. Approved revisions are locked and every revision keeps a snapshot, so you can show a surveyor or client exactly which revision applied.

Marine work often asks for procedures written to class society rules as well as to ASME or AWS references for industrial work, and a Jacksonville contractor may maintain both for the same method. The workflow runs draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejected and archived states, and records who prepared, reviewed and approved each revision and when. Rejections carry a reason, and approvers get email reminders.

An AI-assisted first draft produces a starting procedure from method, material and standard, falling back to a built-in template. A Level III still reviews and approves everything before it is published. NCR and CAPA workflows can be configured during implementation for clients who expect corrective actions tracked to closure.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Jacksonville jobs

Quotations carry job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, with NDT services flagged by method and category, a branded PDF and online acceptance and signature that converts to a sales order. Invoices then draw on the job's timesheets, equipment and consumables.

Marine work is often billed by the day or shift with standby while a tank is ventilated or a hold is cleaned, while terminal and plant work may be quoted by scope. The invoice header records the NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with labour, equipment and consumables subtotals. Lines carry cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours. Timesheets record work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), billable flag and rate multiplier, so night and weekend shifts on a vessel with a tight sailing date are billed correctly. Field expenses can be re-billed to the job through Expenses.

The financial dashboard covers revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, outstanding invoices, bills and expenses across 12 months. Taxes are configured during implementation, and the open REST API links to QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation.

Winning more Jacksonville work: CRM and dashboards

The CRM records service line, lead source, NDT service type, industry sector, site country, and estimated technicians and days, with a lead score from 0 to 100 grouped as hot, warm, nurture or cold. For a contractor chasing ship repair, terminal and plant work, it shows which enquiries are worth a site visit.

Leads import from CSV, AI-personalised email previews speed up follow-up, and drip sequences by service line keep marine and industrial contacts on separate tracks. The Business Cards feature turns a photographed card from a port or maritime event into a CRM lead. Dashboards show calibration due and overdue, certificates expiring and expired, and issued equipment overdue, next to the financials.

Implementing the Atlantis ERP in Jacksonville

Atlantis NDT implements remotely, scheduled around Eastern time, and works around vessel schedules so a rollout does not collide with a ship in the yard.

  1. Discovery. We review your marine and industrial service lines, class society clients, report formats and dispatch.
  2. Data load. Technicians, certificates, vision tests, instruments, calibration certificates, clients and open jobs come across from spreadsheets.
  3. Configuration. Marine report mode, templates, numbering, procedure register, quote and invoice layouts, alerts and integrations are set up.
  4. Pilot. One vessel job and one land job run end to end.
  5. Go live and support. The team moves over, with Atlantis on hand for changes.

Anything that is not built in is configured during implementation. The eLearning portal and the Practical NDT 3D simulator can be added for trainees, and Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT software for marine inspection in Jacksonville?

Choose software that produces class-ready report packages and also runs dispatch, certificates and invoicing. The Atlantis ERP has a marine mode that merges class, Level II and calibration certificates into the report PDF.

Which classification societies are supported?

The marine library includes DNV, ABS, Lloyd's Register, BV, RINA, IRS and ClassNK.

Can technicians write reports inside tanks with no signal?

Yes. The offline field app stores drafts and photos locally and syncs when back in coverage.

Is it suitable for a small NDT company?

Yes. Switch on only the apps you need; pricing is quote on request.

Can it connect to our accounting system?

Yes. The open REST API integrates with QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo and other systems that accept API connections, scoped per implementation.

Does the ERP calculate corrosion rates from thickness readings?

No. The ERP records thickness readings in reports; it does not calculate corrosion rates. Thickness trends can be visualised in Atlantis Digital Twins.

Ask a question about the Atlantis ERP in Jacksonville and we will arrange a demo.
